Both black holes and confined quarks satisfy similar axioms regarding information encoding on boundaries, entropy-area relationships, and the emergence of thermodynamic properties from underlying dynamics.

decisions.choice: Differential geometry, Information theory, Dynamical systems
decisions.reasoning: Differential geometry provides the mathematical structure for horizons in GR (event horizons, cosmological horizons) and confinement surfaces in particle physics. Information theory formalizes entropy and information loss, while dynamical systems capture the time evolution and thermalization behavior near these boundaries.

decisions.choice: Systems with horizons or confinement scales naturally partition into accessible and inaccessible degrees of freedom. Tracing over the inaccessible sector produces entropy proportional to the boundary area (via holographic arguments), while generic dynamics causes information to flow across the boundary, leading to apparent information loss and thermalization of the accessible sector with temperature determined by the horizon's surface gravity or confinement strength.
